title: Used to / Would / Be Used to — Advanced

questions.def: "Used to" describes a past habit that is no longer true.
questions.question: She ___ go to the library every Saturday, but now she streams films.

questions.def: "Be used to" describes something familiar and not unusual.
questions.question: I ___ living in the countryside; it's very peaceful.

questions.def: "Used to" + infinitive expresses a past habit or state.
questions.question: I ___ in London before moving to Rome.

questions.def: "Would" describes a past habit, especially storytelling.
questions.question: When I was a child, my grandfather ___ tell me stories.

questions.def: "Be used to" describes being accustomed to something.
questions.question: They ___ the noise of the city after living here so long.

questions.def: "Would" can describe past habits, especially in narratives.
questions.question: He ___ late when he had that project.

questions.def: "Used to" describes a past state that is no longer true.
questions.question: We ___ have a garden, but now we live in an apartment.

questions.def: "Be used to" questions about familiarity with something.
questions.question: Are you ___ driving on the left in the UK?

questions.def: "Would" describes past habits, especially recurring events.
questions.question: They ___ dinner at 6 PM when they were children.

questions.def: "Used to" describes a past preference that has changed.
questions.question: I never ___ like broccoli, but now I love it.

questions.def: "Be used to" describes being accustomed to a routine.
questions.question: She ___ the early mornings; she's a nurse.

questions.def: The correct form is "used to" not "use to".
questions.question: He use to playing the piano every day after school.

questions.def: "Used to" + infinitive describes a past habit.
questions.question: He ___ to work, but now he drives.

questions.def: "Would" describes recurring past actions, like knitting sweaters.
questions.question: My grandmother ___ knit sweaters for us every Christmas.

questions.def: "Be used to" describes being accustomed to a flavor.
questions.question: They ___ the spicy food after living in India.

questions.def: "Used to" + infinitive describes a past habit.
questions.question: We ___ to the beach every summer.

questions.def: "Used to" describes a past feeling that has changed.
questions.question: He ___ be afraid of heights, but he's a climber now.

questions.def: "Be used to" describes being accustomed to cold.
questions.question: She ___ the cold weather after living in Alaska.

questions.def: "Would" + infinitive, no extra "to".
questions.question: He would to visit his grandmother every Sunday afternoon.

questions.def: "Would" describes recurring past actions, like swimming.
questions.question: They ___ in the lake every morning.

questions.def: "Used to" describes a past habit that is no longer true.
questions.question: I ___ smoke, but I quit five years ago.

questions.def: "Be used to" questions about familiarity with something.
questions.question: Are you ___ the new software yet?

questions.def: "Would" describes regular past habits.
questions.question: She ___ the violin every day after school.

questions.def: "Used to" describes a past state that is no longer true.
questions.question: He ___ be a doctor, but he retired last year.

questions.def: "Be used to" describes being accustomed to a flavor.
questions.question: They ___ the taste of durian.

questions.def: 'Used to' is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He used to ___ early, but now he doesn't.

questions.def: 'Get used to' means to become accustomed to something.
questions.question: She ___ to the noise after a while.

questions.def: It should be 'I am used to', meaning I'm accustomed to it.
questions.question: I am use to working long hours now.

questions.def: 'Used to' indicates a past habit or state.
questions.question: He ___ in London before moving to Rome.

questions.def: 'Would' can describe past habitual actions.
questions.question: When I was a child, I ___ spend hours reading.
